Let \( A_1, A_2, A_3, \ldots \) be a sequence of finite nonempty sets of positive integers. Given that \( |A_i \cap A_j| = \gcd(i, j) \) for all (not necessarily distinct) positive integers \( i \) and \( j \), compute the minimum possible value of

\[
\sum_{d|250} \max A_d,
\]

where the sum ranges over all positive integer divisors \( d \) of 250.

(For a finite nonempty set \( S \), we define \( \max S \) as the largest element of \( S \).)


Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

Let \(m_d=\max A_d\) for \(d\mid 250\). The divisors of \(250\) are  
\[
1,2,5,10,25,50,125,250.
\]

Taking \(i=j\) in the given condition gives
\[
|A_i|=\gcd(i,i)=i.
\]
So \(m_d\ge d\) for every divisor \(d\).

Also,
\[
|A_d\cup A_e|
=|A_d|+|A_e|-|A_d\cap A_e|
=d+e-\gcd(d,e).
\]
If \(\max(m_d,m_e)\le t\), then \(A_d\cup A_e\subseteq\{1,\dots,t\}\), so
\[
\max(m_d,m_e)\ge |A_d\cup A_e|.
\]

Now apply this to the pairs we need:

- \(m_1\ge 1\).
- For \(2,5\): union size \(2+5-1=6\). With \(m_2\ge2,m_5\ge5\) and \(\max(m_2,m_5)\ge6\), we get \(m_2+m_5\ge8\).
- For \(10,25\): union size \(10+25-5=30\). With \(m_{10}\ge10,m_{25}\ge25\) and \(\max(m_{10},m_{25})\ge30\), we get \(m_{10}+m_{25}\ge40\).
- For \(50,125\): union size \(50+125-25=150\). With \(m_{50}\ge50,m_{125}\ge125\) and \(\max(m_{50},m_{125})\ge150\), we get \(m_{50}+m_{125}\ge200\).
- \(m_{250}\ge250\).

Thus
\[
\sum_{d\mid250} m_d
\ge 1+8+40+200+250=499.
\]

It remains to show \(499\) is attainable. Use the standard construction: for each \(r\), take exactly \(\varphi(r)\) elements of “type \(r\),” where type \(r\) elements appear precisely in those \(A_i\) with \(r\mid i\). Then
\[
|A_i\cap A_j|=\sum_{r\mid\gcd(i,j)}\varphi(r)=\gcd(i,j).
\]

Assign labels to the relevant types as follows:

\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
\text{type }r & \text{labels}\\
\hline
1 & 1\\
2 & 2\\
5 & 3,4,5,6\\
10 & 7,8,9,10\\
25 & 11,\dots,30\\
50 & 31,\dots,50\\
125 & 51,\dots,150\\
250 & 151,\dots,250
\end{array}
\]

All other types receive labels \(251,252,\dots\). Then the relevant maxima are

\[
\begin{array}{c|cccccccc}
d&1&2&5&10&25&50&125&250\\
\hline
m_d&1&2&6&10&30&50&150&250
\end{array}
\]

whose sum is
\[
1+2+6+10+30+50+150+250=499.
\]

Therefore the minimum possible value is

\[
\boxed{499}
\]
